I ported the program to Kotlin in `src/main/kotlin/WordFreq.kt`, using only the standard library. `build.sh` compiles it into a jar and writes `./app`, a small script that runs it with `java`. Counting works the same way as the original: words are lower-cased in place and tracked in a hash table that points back into the input, so no string is created per word.

`node check.mjs` passes all 6 example cases on a clean build. I also compared it against the original Node program on a 50 MB gen
